rationale: This ethnographic and historical study examines speculative state planning, bureaucratic practices, and informal labor relations at the Kolkata Port Trust along the Hooghly River. It does not examine household or community water supply or sanitation services (failing Criterion 1) or any water/sanitation access outcomes (failing Criterion 4), warranting exclusion for wrong topic (E01).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although the study examines administrative and governance practices under a literal reading of Criterion 2 (state planning, bureaucracy, and public-private partnerships at the Kolkata Port Trust), it is excluded under both readings because it concerns port governance and informal river labor rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: This article examines the forms of state planning associated with neoliberalism, through a history and ethnography of the Kolkata Port Trust during liberalization.
This new mode of rule is particularly problematic in settings such as the Hooghly River, where informality dominates in labor relationships.
